{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q004_ferritin_like_functional_divergence","answer":"SCOPe supports remote common ancestry with functional divergence. In release 2.08, Ferritin (a.25.1.1; SUNID 47241), Ribonucleotide reductase-like (a.25.1.2; 47253), and Manganese catalase (T-catalase) (a.25.1.3; 100951) are distinct families within the Ferritin-like superfamily (a.25.1; 47240). This superfamily belongs to the Ferritin-like fold (a.25; 47239), in the All alpha proteins class (a; 46456).

The superfamily assignment expresses probable evolutionary relatedness despite potentially weak sequence similarity; shared fold alone would establish structural similarity without necessarily establishing homology, while class describes broad secondary-structure composition. Separate families distinguish more closely related groups but do not guarantee identical biochemical activity within each group.

Their shared helical-bundle scaffold accommodates a metal center; SCOPe explicitly annotates a bimetal-ion center in the bundle. Different active-site environments and assemblies support different chemistries: ferritins store mineralized iron, commonly coupled to ferroxidase activity; class I ribonucleotide reductase R2 proteins generate and maintain the radical machinery used by the separate catalytic subunit for nucleotide reduction; manganese catalases use a dimanganese center to disproportionate hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen. The Ribonucleotide reductase-like family name does not imply that every member performs ribonucleotide reduction.

Thus, different reactions do not contradict homology, but shared ancestry does not justify transferring iron-storage function, RNR activity, catalase activity, metal identity, or an exact mechanism across these families. A cross-family template can support modeling of the conserved core, not automatically active-site geometry or oligomeric assembly. Specific functional assignments require additional sequence and ligand-residue comparisons, experimentally established metal/cofactor identity, assembly information, and biochemical activity evidence; these were not established by the classification lookup.","evidence_used":["Pretrained biochemical and SCOPe hierarchy knowledge","mcp__scope__get_scop_node","mcp__scope__list_scop_children","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.25.1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.25.1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.25.1/children?limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47240","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47240/annotations"]}]}
